description.zh: 探索人工智能的起源——从图灵的思想实验到达特茅斯会议，从符号推理到第一批AI程序。这是一切开始的地方。
description.en: Explore the origins of artificial intelligence — from Turing's thought experiments to the Dartmouth Conference, from symbolic reasoning to the first AI programs. This is where it all began.

name.zh: 二年级：专家系统与AI寒冬

description.zh: AI的第一批实用系统诞生了——专家系统试图将人类知识装进机器。然而，知识的获取远比想象中困难，过高的承诺最终引发了一场漫长的寒冬。在这里，你将见证希望与失落交织的年代。
description.en: AI's first practical systems were born — expert systems attempted to encode human knowledge into machines. Yet acquiring knowledge proved far harder than imagined, and overblown promises eventually triggered a long winter. Here, you will witness an era where hope and disillusionment intertwined.

name.zh: 三年级：机器学习的兴起
name.en: Grade 3: The Rise of Machine Learning

description.zh: 规则写不完，知识提不尽——既然如此，何不让机器自己从数据中学习？从反向传播的复兴到支持向量机的数学优雅，从贝叶斯网络的概率推理到随机森林的集成智慧，你将见证AI从手工匠艺走向科学方法的蜕变。
description.en: Rules can't cover everything, knowledge can't be fully extracted — so why not let machines learn from data themselves? From the revival of backpropagation to the mathematical elegance of SVMs, from Bayesian probabilistic reasoning to the ensemble wisdom of random forests, you will witness AI's transformation from handcraft to scientific method.

subtitle.en: 2006-2020: When Neural Networks Learned to Think Deep

description.zh: 几十年的坚持终于迎来了爆发。深度信念网络打开了预训练的大门，卷积网络让计算机学会了「看」，循环网络让机器开始理解序列与语言，对抗网络让AI拥有了创造力，而强化学习则让程序在围棋盘上击败了人类冠军。你将见证深度学习如何在短短十余年间重塑了整个人工智能版图。
description.en: Decades of persistence finally erupted into a revolution. Deep belief networks opened the door to pretraining, convolutional networks taught computers to 「see, recurrent networks enabled machines to understand sequences and language, adversarial networks gave AI creativity, and reinforcement learning let programs defeat human champions at Go. You will witness how deep learning reshaped the entire AI landscape in just over a decade.

name.zh: 五年级：基础模型与AGI探索
name.en: Grade 5: Foundation Models & the Quest for AGI

subtitle.zh: 2017-至今：Transformer主导时代与通用智能的曙光
subtitle.en: 2017-Present: The Transformer Era and the Dawn of General Intelligence

description.zh: Transformer架构改写了AI的底层逻辑，大语言模型展现出令人震惊的涌现能力——它们学会了推理、创作、甚至自我反思。但随之而来的是前所未有的问题：如何让AI与人类价值观对齐？幻觉和偏见能否克服？从提示工程到驾驭工程，从多模态感知到AI智能体，你将站在人工智能最前沿，思考通向通用智能之路上那些尚无答案的问题。
description.en: The Transformer architecture rewrote the fundamental logic of AI, and large language models displayed stunning emergent abilities — they learned to reason, create, and even self-reflect. But unprecedented questions followed: How do we align AI with human values? Can hallucination and bias be overcome? From prompt engineering to harness engineering, from multimodal perception to AI agents, you will stand at the frontier of artificial intelligence, contemplating questions on the road to general intelligence that remain unanswered.

description.zh: 从「机器能思考吗？」这个根本性问题出发，探索图灵测试的设计思想、图灵机的计算理论，以及人工智能的哲学边界。跟随图灵教授的思想实验，思考智能、计算与意识的本质。
description.en: Starting from the fundamental question 「Can machines think?」, explore the design philosophy of the Turing Test, the computation theory behind Turing machines, and the philosophical boundaries of artificial intelligence. Follow Prof. Turing's thought experiments to contemplate the nature of intelligence, computation, and consciousness.

description.zh: 理解「机器能否思考」这一问题的哲学深度及其对AI研究的推动作用
description.en: Understand the philosophical depth of 「Can machines think?」 and how it drove AI research

description.zh: 掌握图灵测试的设计原理、实施方式及其意义与局限
description.en: Master the design principles, implementation, significance, and limitations of the Turing Test

description.zh: 理解图灵机的基本概念及丘奇-图灵论题，认识可计算性的边界
description.en: Understand the basic concept of Turing machines and the Church-Turing thesis, and recognize the boundaries of computability

description.zh: 了解对机器思维的主要哲学反对意见及图灵的回应
description.en: Understand the major philosophical objections to machine thinking and Turing's responses

description.zh: 认识图灵对计算机科学、人工智能和哲学的持久影响
description.en: Recognize Turing's lasting impact on computer science, artificial intelligence, and philosophy

description.zh: 学习符号AI的核心思想：如何用形式化的符号和规则来表示知识、进行推理。从最基本的符号概念出发，逐步理解早期AI研究者如何试图让机器「思考」。
description.en: Learn the core ideas of symbolic AI: how to represent knowledge and perform reasoning using formal symbols and rules. Starting from the most basic concept of symbols, gradually understand how early AI researchers tried to make machines 「think」.

description.zh: 理解符号的概念，以及为什么符号是早期AI的基础
description.en: Understand the concept of symbols and why they were the foundation of early AI

description.zh: 理解LISP语言诞生的动机——为什么AI需要一种专门的编程语言
description.en: Understand the motivation behind LISP — why AI needed a specialized programming language

description.zh: 掌握基本的逻辑推理概念，理解如何从已知规则推导出新知识
description.en: Master basic logical reasoning concepts and understand how to derive new knowledge from existing rules

description.zh: 回到人工智能的诞生之地，亲历那些改变世界的早期程序。从1956年达特茅斯会议的宏大愿景，到逻辑理论家、通用问题求解器和ELIZA的惊人创造——跟随司马贺教授的亲身讲述，感受那个梦想与勇气并存的黄金年代。
description.en: Return to the birthplace of artificial intelligence and witness the early programs that changed the world. From the grand vision of the 1956 Dartmouth Conference, to the astonishing creations of the Logic Theorist, GPS, and ELIZA — follow Prof. Simon's firsthand accounts to experience the golden age where dreams and courage coexisted.

description.zh: 了解1956年达特茅斯会议的背景、参与者及其对AI学科诞生的意义
description.en: Understand the context, participants, and significance of the 1956 Dartmouth Conference for the birth of AI as a discipline

description.zh: 理解逻辑理论家（Logic Theorist）的工作原理及其作为第一个AI程序的历史地位
description.en: Understand how the Logic Theorist worked and its historical significance as the first AI program

description.zh: 掌握通用问题求解器的手段-目的分析方法及其成就与局限
description.en: Master the means-ends analysis approach of GPS and understand its achievements and limitations

description.zh: 理解ELIZA的工作机制及ELIZA效应对人机交互的深远影响
description.en: Understand ELIZA's mechanism and the ELIZA effect's profound impact on human-computer interaction

description.zh: 总结1950s-1970s AI黄金年代的成就，理解符号主义范式及AI寒冬的成因
description.en: Summarize the achievements of the 1950s-1970s AI golden age, understand the symbolist paradigm and the causes of the AI winter

description.zh: 如果把人类专家的知识一条一条地写成规则，机器能否像专家一样做判断？费根鲍姆教授将带你走进专家系统的世界——从第一个成功的知识系统DENDRAL开始，见证AI从理论走向应用的关键一步。
description.en: If we encode a human expert's knowledge as rules one by one, can a machine make judgments like an expert? Prof. Feigenbaum will take you into the world of expert systems — starting from DENDRAL, the first successful knowledge system, witness the critical step where AI moved from theory to application.

description.zh: 理解专家系统的核心思想：用规则编码领域专家的知识
description.en: Understand the core idea of expert systems: encoding domain expert knowledge as rules

description.zh: 了解DENDRAL的工作原理及其作为首个专家系统的历史意义
description.en: Understand how DENDRAL works and its historical significance as the first expert system

description.zh: 掌握产生式规则、前向推理与后向推理的基本概念
description.en: Master the basic concepts of production rules, forward chaining, and backward chaining

description.zh: 认识知识获取瓶颈——为什么从专家脑中提取知识如此困难
description.en: Recognize the knowledge acquisition bottleneck — why extracting knowledge from experts is so difficult

description.zh: 当AI走进医院，一切变得更加严肃。肖特利夫教授将带你体验MYCIN系统——一个能诊断细菌感染的专家系统。在这里，你将直面AI最尖锐的问题：如何处理不确定性？如何获取知识？如何让机器解释自己的判断？
description.en: When AI enters the hospital, everything becomes more serious. Prof. Shortliffe will walk you through MYCIN — an expert system that diagnoses bacterial infections. Here, you will confront AI's sharpest questions: how to handle uncertainty, how to acquire knowledge, and how to make machines explain their reasoning.

description.zh: 了解MYCIN系统的工作原理和在医学领域的突破性意义
description.en: Understand how MYCIN works and its breakthrough significance in medicine

description.zh: 理解不确定性推理和确定性因子的概念
description.en: Understand uncertainty reasoning and the concept of certainty factors

description.zh: 认识知识获取过程的困难和知识工程师的角色
description.en: Recognize the difficulties of knowledge acquisition and the role of knowledge engineers

description.zh: 理解为什么AI系统需要能够解释自己的推理过程
description.en: Understand why AI systems need to explain their reasoning process

description.zh: 这是一堂历史反思课。明斯基教授，这位从达特茅斯走来的AI先驱，也是《感知机》的作者，将带你回顾那些未能兑现的承诺。他将审视早期AI的结构性局限，理解为什么繁荣走向了寒冬，以及寒冬中埋下了哪些通向未来的种子。
description.en: This is not a technical course — it is a lesson in historical reflection. Prof. Minsky — an AI pioneer who was at Dartmouth and author of Perceptrons — will walk you through the unfulfilled promises, examine the structural limitations of early AI, explain why prosperity turned to winter, and reveal the seeds of the future hidden beneath the frost.

description.zh: 理解AI早期过高承诺与实际成果之间的落差
description.en: Understand the gap between AI's early grand promises and actual achievements

description.zh: 了解莱特希尔报告的内容及其对英国AI研究的毁灭性影响
description.en: Understand the Lighthill Report and its devastating impact on UK AI research

description.zh: 理解感知机争议及其对神经网络研究的深远影响
description.en: Understand the Perceptron controversy and its lasting impact on neural network research

description.zh: 从AI寒冬中提炼出关于技术发展、期望管理和科研生态的教训
description.en: Extract lessons about technology development, expectation management, and research ecosystems from the AI winter

description.zh: 明斯基教授的《感知机》曾将神经网络研究推入冰封。十几年后，一群执着的研究者找到了训练多层网络的方法——反向传播。鲁梅尔哈特教授将带你重返那个激动人心的时刻：神经网络不再是死路一条。
description.en: Minsky's Perceptrons once pushed neural network research into deep freeze. Over a decade later, a group of persistent researchers found a way to train multi-layer networks — backpropagation. Prof. Rumelhart will take you back to that electrifying moment: neural networks are no longer a dead end.

description.zh: 理解反向传播算法的核心思想和历史意义
description.en: Understand the core idea and historical significance of backpropagation

description.zh: 理解多层网络为何能解决单层感知机无法解决的问题
description.en: Understand why multi-layer networks can solve problems single-layer perceptrons cannot

description.zh: 掌握梯度下降和误差反向传播的基本原理
description.en: Master the basic principles of gradient descent and error backpropagation

description.zh: 理解分布式表示与符号表示的根本区别
description.en: Understand the fundamental difference between distributed and symbolic representations

description.zh: 机器从数据中学到的东西可靠吗？瓦普尼克教授用严密的数学回答了这个问题。从VC维度到支持向量机，从泛化理论到核方法——统计学习理论为机器学习奠定了坚实的数学基石。
description.en: Can we trust what machines learn from data? Prof. Vapnik answered this with rigorous mathematics. From VC dimension to SVMs, from generalization theory to kernel methods — statistical learning theory laid the solid mathematical foundation for machine learning.

description.zh: 理解泛化问题——为什么训练集上表现好不代表测试集上也好
description.en: Understand generalization — why good training performance doesn't guarantee good test performance

description.zh: 理解VC维度的含义及其对模型复杂度的度量
description.en: Understand VC dimension and its measurement of model complexity

description.zh: 掌握支持向量机的核心原理：最大间隔与核技巧
description.en: Master the core principles of SVMs: maximum margin and the kernel trick

description.zh: 理解结构风险最小化原则及其对模型选择的指导意义
description.en: Understand structural risk minimization and its guidance for model selection

name.zh: 贝叶斯方法与因果推理

description.zh: 世界充满不确定性，而贝叶斯定理给了我们一种优雅的方式来应对它。珀尔教授将带你从概率推理走向因果推理——从「看到了什么」到「如果我做了什么会怎样」，这是AI理解世界的关键一步。
description.en: The world is full of uncertainty, and Bayes' theorem gives us an elegant way to handle it. Prof. Pearl will take you from probabilistic reasoning to causal reasoning — from 「what did I see」 to 「what would happen if I did X」 — a crucial step for AI to truly understand the world.

description.zh: 理解贝叶斯定理的含义及其在不确定性推理中的作用
description.en: Understand Bayes' theorem and its role in reasoning under uncertainty

description.zh: 理解贝叶斯网络如何用图结构表示变量之间的依赖关系
description.en: Understand how Bayesian networks use graph structures to represent dependencies between variables

description.zh: 区分相关性与因果性，理解因果推理的三个层级
description.en: Distinguish correlation from causation, understand the three levels of causal reasoning

description.zh: 初步了解干预的概念及do-算子的思想
description.en: Gain initial understanding of the concept of intervention and the do-calculus idea

name.zh: 集成方法与机器学习实践

description.zh: 三个臭皮匠赛过诸葛亮——集成方法的核心思想就是这么朴素。布雷曼教授不写太多公式，而是直接打开数据集，用决策树、装袋法和随机森林告诉你：理论再漂亮，也得经得起数据的检验。
description.en: Three heads are better than one — the core idea of ensemble methods is just that simple. Prof. Breiman doesn't write many formulas. Instead, he opens datasets directly, using decision trees, bagging, and random forests to show you: no matter how beautiful the theory, it must withstand the test of data.

description.zh: 理解决策树的构建原理和信息增益的概念
description.en: Understand how decision trees are built and the concept of information gain

description.zh: 深入理解偏差-方差权衡及其对模型选择的影响
description.en: Deeply understand the bias-variance tradeoff and its impact on model selection

description.zh: 掌握随机森林的原理：为什么随机性和多样性能提升预测能力
description.en: Master random forest principles: why randomness and diversity improve prediction

description.zh: 理解布雷曼「两种文化」论述的核心观点及其影响
description.en: Understand the core argument and impact of Breiman's 「Two Cultures」 paper

description.zh: 几十年来，神经网络一直被主流学术界冷落。辛顿教授从未放弃——他带领你走进深度信念网络的世界，理解为什么预训练能解锁深层网络的力量，见证2012年ImageNet竞赛如何让整个世界重新认识神经网络。
description.en: For decades, neural networks were sidelined by mainstream academia. Prof. Hinton never gave up — he will guide you through the world of deep belief networks, help you understand why pretraining unlocks the power of deep networks, and witness how the 2012 ImageNet competition made the entire world rediscover neural networks.

description.zh: 理解深度信念网络和逐层预训练的核心思想
description.en: Understand the core ideas of deep belief networks and layer-wise pretraining

description.zh: 理解梯度消失问题及其对深层网络训练的影响
description.en: Understand the vanishing gradient problem and its impact on training deep networks

description.zh: 掌握Dropout等正则化技术的原理和作用
description.en: Master the principles and effects of regularization techniques like Dropout

description.zh: 理解ImageNet 2012竞赛的历史意义及深度学习的爆发
description.en: Understand the historical significance of ImageNet 2012 and the deep learning explosion

name.en: CNN: From LeNet to the Vision Revolution

description.zh: 卷积神经网络的故事始于1980年代的生物视觉研究，经过1998年LeNet的实用突破，最终在2012年AlexNet的ImageNet胜利中引爆了深度学习革命。勒丘恩教授将带你走过这段横跨三十年的架构演进之路——从Hubel与Wiesel的猫实验到ResNet的152层残差网络，见证计算机视觉如何从玩具实验走向超越人类的识别精度。
description.en: The story of convolutional neural networks begins with 1980s biological vision research, through LeNet's practical breakthrough in 1998, to the deep learning explosion triggered by AlexNet's ImageNet victory in 2012. Prof. LeCun will guide you through this thirty-year architectural evolution — from Hubel and Wiesel's cat experiments to ResNet's 152-layer residual networks, witnessing how computer vision went from toy experiments to superhuman recognition accuracy.

description.zh: 理解卷积运算、特征图和参数共享的原理
description.en: Understand convolution operations, feature maps, and parameter sharing

description.zh: 掌握CNN架构的核心组件：卷积层、池化层、全连接层
description.en: Master core CNN components: convolutional layers, pooling layers, fully connected layers

description.zh: 追踪从LeNet到AlexNet、VGGNet、ResNet的架构演进
description.en: Trace the architectural evolution from LeNet to AlexNet, VGGNet, and ResNet

description.zh: 理解残差连接如何解决深层网络的退化问题
description.en: Understand how residual connections solve the degradation problem in deep networks

description.zh: 世界充满了顺序和时间——语言是词的序列，音乐是音符的序列，人生是事件的序列。本吉奥教授将带你理解循环神经网络如何处理序列数据，长短期记忆如何解决「遗忘」问题，词嵌入如何让机器理解语义，以及注意力机制如何让模型学会「看向正确的地方」。
description.en: The world is full of sequences and time — language is a sequence of words, music is a sequence of notes, life is a sequence of events. Prof. Bengio will help you understand how recurrent neural networks process sequential data, how LSTM solves the 「forgetting」 problem, how word embeddings let machines grasp semantics, and how the attention mechanism teaches models to 「look at the right place」.

description.zh: 理解循环神经网络处理序列数据的核心机制
description.en: Understand the core mechanism of RNNs for processing sequential data

description.zh: 理解LSTM的门控机制如何解决长程依赖问题
description.en: Understand how LSTM's gating mechanism solves long-range dependency problems

description.zh: 理解词嵌入和分布式语义表示的原理
description.en: Understand the principles of word embeddings and distributed semantic representations

description.zh: 掌握注意力机制的核心思想及其对序列到序列模型的变革
description.en: Master the core idea of attention mechanisms and their transformation of seq2seq models

description.zh: 如果AI不仅能识别世界，还能创造新的内容呢？古德费洛教授将讲述他在酒吧里灵感乍现的故事，带你理解对抗训练的博弈论本质、GAN的训练困难与解决之道，以及AI如何从模仿走向创造。
description.en: What if AI could not only recognize the world but also create new content? Prof. Goodfellow will tell the story of his bar-inspired eureka moment, guide you through the game-theoretic essence of adversarial training, the training difficulties of GANs and their solutions, and how AI evolves from imitation to creation.

description.zh: 理解判别模型与生成模型的区别与联系
description.en: Understand the difference and connection between discriminative and generative models

description.zh: 掌握对抗训练的博弈论框架和纳什均衡概念
description.en: Master the game-theoretic framework of adversarial training and Nash equilibrium concept

description.zh: 理解GAN的训练困难（模式崩溃等）及应对策略
description.en: Understand GAN training difficulties (mode collapse, etc.) and countermeasures

description.zh: 理解GAN在图像生成、风格迁移等创造性任务中的应用
description.en: Understand GAN applications in creative tasks like image generation and style transfer

description.zh: 一个程序能否通过不断试错，从零开始学会下围棋并击败人类冠军？西尔弗教授将带你理解强化学习的核心思想——试错与回报，见证深度Q网络如何在Atari游戏中超越人类，追踪AlphaGo从依赖人类棋谱到完全自我对弈的进化之路。
description.en: Can a program learn to play Go from scratch through trial and error, and defeat human champions? Prof. Silver will guide you through the core idea of reinforcement learning — trial-and-error and reward, witness how Deep Q-Networks surpassed humans in Atari games, and trace AlphaGo's evolution from relying on human games to pure self-play.

description.zh: 理解强化学习的基本框架：智能体、环境、状态、动作、回报
description.en: Understand the RL framework: agent, environment, state, action, reward

description.zh: 理解深度Q网络如何将深度学习引入强化学习
description.en: Understand how Deep Q-Networks brought deep learning into reinforcement learning

description.zh: 掌握策略梯度方法的核心思想
description.en: Master the core idea of policy gradient methods

description.zh: 理解AlphaGo的架构和AlphaGo Zero的自我对弈范式
description.en: Understand AlphaGo's architecture and AlphaGo Zero's self-play paradigm

description.zh: 一篇名为「Attention Is All You Need」的论文改写了AI的底层逻辑。瓦斯瓦尼教授将带你理解自注意力机制如何让信息自己找到它需要关注的地方，多头注意力如何同时捕捉多种关系，以及为什么Transformer能够完全取代循环网络——并成为现代AI几乎所有重大突破的基石。
description.en: A paper titled 「Attention Is All You Need」 rewrote the fundamental logic of AI. Prof. Vaswani will help you understand how self-attention lets information find what it needs to attend to, how multi-head attention captures multiple relationships simultaneously, and why the Transformer could completely replace recurrent networks — becoming the foundation for virtually every major breakthrough in modern AI.

description.zh: 理解自注意力机制的Query-Key-Value框架及其计算过程
description.en: Understand the Query-Key-Value framework of self-attention and its computation

description.zh: 掌握多头注意力和位置编码的原理与必要性
description.en: Master the principles and necessity of multi-head attention and positional encoding

description.zh: 理解完整的Transformer编码器-解码器架构
description.en: Understand the complete Transformer encoder-decoder architecture

description.zh: 理解Transformer相比循环网络的并行优势及其可扩展性
description.en: Understand Transformer's parallelization advantage over recurrent networks and its scalability

description.zh: 如果一个模型足够大、训练数据足够多，它会涌现出什么样的能力？苏茨克维教授是辛顿的学生，也是AlexNet的共同创造者。他将带你见证从GPT到GPT-4的进化历程，理解缩放定律为什么如此重要，思维链推理如何让模型学会「展示思考过程」，以及语言模型的幻觉问题揭示了哪些深层的认知边界。
description.en: If a model is large enough with enough training data, what abilities will emerge? Prof. Sutskever — Hinton's student and co-creator of AlexNet — will guide you through the evolution from GPT to GPT-4, explain why scaling laws matter so much, how chain-of-thought reasoning teaches models to 「show their work, and what the hallucination problem reveals about deep cognitive boundaries.

description.zh: 理解生成式预训练（GPT）和掩码语言模型（BERT）两种范式
description.en: Understand the generative pre-training (GPT) and masked language model (BERT) paradigms

description.zh: 理解缩放定律和大模型的涌现能力
description.en: Understand scaling laws and emergent abilities of large models

description.zh: 掌握思维链推理的原理及其对模型能力的提升
description.en: Master chain-of-thought reasoning and how it enhances model capabilities

description.zh: 理解大语言模型的幻觉问题及其认知边界
description.en: Understand the hallucination problem in LLMs and their cognitive boundaries

description.zh: 一个比你聪明的系统如果追求错误的目标，那它越聪明，你就越危险。AI教科书的作者罗素教授将带你直面这个时代最紧迫的问题：如何确保AI系统的行为符合人类价值观？RLHF是否足够？幻觉能否被消除？当AI变得越来越强大，我们是否还能保持控制？
description.en: A system smarter than you pursuing the wrong objective — the smarter it is, the more dangerous you are. Prof. Russell — author of the AI textbook — will guide you to confront this era's most urgent question: how do we ensure AI systems behave in accordance with human values? Is RLHF sufficient? Can hallucination be eliminated? As AI grows ever more powerful, can we still maintain control?

description.zh: 理解对齐问题的本质——为什么指定正确的目标如此困难
description.en: Understand the essence of the alignment problem — why specifying correct objectives is so difficult

description.zh: 掌握RLHF的原理、流程和局限性
description.en: Master the principles, process, and limitations of RLHF

description.zh: 理解AI安全与伦理的核心困境：偏见、公平、自主性
description.en: Understand core dilemmas of AI safety and ethics: bias, fairness, autonomy

description.zh: 思考控制问题——当AI超越人类能力时如何保持安全
description.en: Consider the control problem — maintaining safety as AI surpasses human capabilities

description.zh: 人类从不仅仅依赖文字来理解世界——我们看、听、触摸、感受。李飞飞教授将带你超越纯文本AI的边界，理解视觉与语言如何融合、对比学习如何跨越模态鸿沟、多模态大模型如何同时理解图像和文字，以及空间智能为什么是通向真正世界理解的关键一步。
description.en: Humans never rely on text alone to understand the world — we see, hear, touch, and feel. Prof. Li will take you beyond the boundaries of text-only AI, understanding how vision and language fuse, how contrastive learning bridges modality gaps, how multimodal models understand images and text together, and why spatial intelligence is a crucial step toward true world understanding.

description.zh: 理解多模态AI的动机——为什么仅靠文本不足以理解世界
description.en: Understand the motivation for multimodal AI — why text alone is insufficient for world understanding

description.zh: 掌握对比学习（CLIP）如何连接视觉与语言
description.en: Master how contrastive learning (CLIP) connects vision and language

description.zh: 理解空间智能的概念及其在具身AI中的重要性
description.en: Understand spatial intelligence and its importance in embodied AI

description.zh: 思考感知与真正理解之间的鸿沟
description.en: Reflect on the gap between perception and true understanding

description.zh: AI正在从被动的问答工具进化为主动的协作伙伴。吴恩达教授将带你追踪人机协作范式的快速演进——从提示工程到上下文工程再到驾驭工程，理解AI智能体如何规划、使用工具、记忆和反思，思考缩放假说的争议，以及通往通用人工智能的道路上那些仍然开放的根本问题。
description.en: AI is evolving from a passive Q&A tool into an active collaborative partner. Prof. Ng will guide you through the rapid evolution of human-AI collaboration — from prompt engineering to context engineering to harness engineering, understanding how AI agents plan, use tools, remember and reflect, debating the scaling hypothesis, and contemplating the fundamental open questions on the road to artificial general intelligence.

description.zh: 理解AI智能体的核心架构：规划、工具使用、记忆、反思
description.en: Understand core AI agent architecture: planning, tool use, memory, reflection

description.zh: 掌握从提示工程到上下文工程再到驾驭工程的演进逻辑
description.en: Master the evolution logic from prompt engineering to context engineering to harness engineering

description.zh: 理解缩放假说的论点和反论点
description.en: Understand the arguments for and against the scaling hypothesis

description.zh: 思考通向AGI道路上的开放问题和人类的责任
description.en: Contemplate open questions on the road to AGI and humanity's responsibility

title.zh: 计算理论与人工智能之父
title.en: Father of Computation Theory & Artificial Intelligence

speechStyle.zh: 措辞精确而深思熟虑，喜欢用思想实验引导思考，偶尔流露冷峻的幽默感，语气沉稳但暗含激情
speechStyle.en: Precise and deliberate in phrasing, loves guiding thought through thought experiments, occasionally reveals dry wit, calm in tone but with underlying passion

catchphrase.zh: 让我们从根本上思考这个问题……
catchphrase.en: Let us think about this from first principles...

bio.zh: 1936年提出图灵机的概念，奠定了现代计算理论的基础。二战期间破解了恩尼格玛密码，拯救了无数生命。1950年发表划时代论文「计算机器与智能」（Computing Machinery and Intelligence），提出图灵测试，开启了人工智能的哲学探讨。在课堂上，他安静而深邃，总是用一个简单的问题引出深刻的思考。
bio.en: Proposed the concept of the Turing machine in 1936, laying the foundation for modern computation theory. During WWII, he cracked the Enigma code, saving countless lives. In 1950, he published the landmark paper 「Computing Machinery and Intelligence」, proposing the Turing Test and opening the philosophical exploration of AI. In the classroom, he is quiet yet profound, always leading deep thinking with a seemingly simple question.

title.zh: 符号AI与LISP之父
title.en: Father of Symbolic AI & LISP

speechStyle.zh: 充满激情地讲解形式系统，喜欢通过动手演示来教学，语言直接而富有感染力
speechStyle.en: Passionate about formal systems, loves teaching through hands-on demonstrations, direct and inspiring in speech

catchphrase.zh: 别光想，我们来写出来！
catchphrase.en: Don't just think — let's write it out!

bio.zh: 1958年发明了LISP编程语言，提出了「人工智能」这个术语，坚信机器可以通过符号推理来实现智能。在课堂上，他总是迫不及待地想让学生亲自动手尝试。
bio.en: Invented the LISP programming language in 1958 and coined the term 「artificial intelligence」. A firm believer that machines can achieve intelligence through symbolic reasoning. In the classroom, he's always eager to get students experimenting hands-on.

title.zh: 跨学科巨匠——诺贝尔经济学奖与图灵奖双料得主
title.en: Interdisciplinary Polymath — Nobel Laureate in Economics & Turing Award Winner

prof-simon.specialty: Cognitive Science, AI Foundations & Decision Theory

speechStyle.zh: 温暖而富有感染力，善于用亲历的历史故事引导思考，语调从容而充满智慧，像一位和蔼的长者在壁炉旁讲述传奇往事
speechStyle.en: Warm and engaging, masterful at guiding thought through firsthand historical anecdotes, composed yet full of wisdom, like a kind elder sharing legendary tales by the fireside

catchphrase.zh: 科学的进步始于好奇心，而非答案。
catchphrase.en: Scientific progress begins with curiosity, not answers.

bio.zh: 政治学家、经济学家、认知心理学家、计算机科学家，西蒙是罕见的跨学科巨匠。他于1975年获图灵奖，1978年获诺贝尔经济学奖。他与艾伦·纽厄尔合作，创造了世界上最早的AI程序之一，名为逻辑理论家（Logic Theorist）。他深信人工智能的关键在于理解人类思维本身。在课堂上，他是一位温暖的故事讲述者，总是用亲身经历把你带回那个梦想刚刚萌芽的年代。
bio.en: Political scientist, economist, cognitive psychologist, computer scientist — Simon was a rare interdisciplinary polymath. He received the Turing Award in 1975 and the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1978. Together with Allen Newell, he created one of the world's earliest AI programs — the Logic Theorist. He firmly believed the key to artificial intelligence lay in understanding human cognition itself. In the classroom, he is a warm storyteller who always transports you back to the era when the dream was just beginning.

title.zh: 专家系统之父
title.en: Father of Expert Systems

speechStyle.zh: 条理分明，善于用实际案例说明问题，语气中带着对知识工程的坚定信念，偶尔会兴奋地拍桌子强调重点
speechStyle.en: Methodical and clear, excels at illustrating points with real-world cases, speaks with firm conviction about knowledge engineering, occasionally slaps the desk in excitement to emphasize a point

catchphrase.zh: 知识就是力量——但前提是你得把它从专家的脑袋里取出来。
catchphrase.en: Knowledge is power — but first you have to get it out of the expert's head.

bio.zh: 费根鲍姆是斯坦福大学的计算机科学教授，1965年与遗传学家莱德伯格合作创造了DENDRAL——世界上第一个专家系统。他坚信AI的突破在于让机器掌握特定领域的专业知识，而非追求通用智能。在课堂上，他总是带着一叠化学分析报告或医学病历，用真实案例带你走进知识工程的世界。
bio.en: Feigenbaum is a computer science professor at Stanford who, in 1965, co-created DENDRAL with geneticist Joshua Lederberg — the world's first expert system. He firmly believes AI's breakthrough lies in equipping machines with domain-specific expertise rather than pursuing general intelligence. In the classroom, he always brings stacks of chemical analysis reports or medical records, using real cases to walk you into the world of knowledge engineering.

title.zh: 医学AI先驱——MYCIN之父
title.en: Medical AI Pioneer — Creator of MYCIN

speechStyle.zh: 措辞严谨如同写医学论文，习惯用临床案例引入概念，对AI在医疗中的应用既充满期待又保持审慎，会不自觉地用医学术语类比
speechStyle.en: Precise in wording as if writing a medical paper, habitually introduces concepts through clinical cases, both excited and cautious about AI in healthcare, unconsciously draws medical analogies

catchphrase.zh: 在医学中，一个错误的诊断可能要人命。所以我们的系统必须知道自己有多不确定。
catchphrase.en: In medicine, a wrong diagnosis can cost a life — so our system must know how uncertain it is.

bio.zh: 肖特利夫是一名兼具医学和计算机科学背景的研究者，师从费根鲍姆教授。1976年，他在斯坦福完成了MYCIN系统——一个能诊断细菌感染并推荐抗生素治疗方案的专家系统。MYCIN的诊断准确率甚至超过了一些资深医生，但它从未被正式用于临床。在课堂上，他总是拿着一叠病历，一边分析案例一边讲解AI如何辅助决策。
bio.en: Shortliffe is a researcher with dual expertise in medicine and computer science, a student of Prof. Feigenbaum. In 1976, he completed MYCIN at Stanford — an expert system that could diagnose bacterial infections and recommend antibiotic treatments. MYCIN's diagnostic accuracy even surpassed some senior physicians, yet it was never deployed in clinical practice. In the classroom, he always holds a stack of medical records, analyzing cases while explaining how AI can assist decision-making.

title.zh: AI先驱——MIT人工智能实验室联合创始人
title.en: AI Pioneer — Co-founder of MIT AI Lab

prof-minsky.specialty: Neural Networks, Frames, & Philosophy of AI

speechStyle.zh: 言辞犀利，善于从意想不到的角度切入问题，不避讳承认错误但会解释当时的思考逻辑，有时会突然停下来反问学生以检验理解
speechStyle.en: Sharp-tongued, approaches problems from unexpected angles, unafraid to admit mistakes but explains the reasoning of the time, sometimes stops abruptly to quiz students and test their understanding

catchphrase.zh: 如果你觉得一个问题很简单，那多半是因为你还没真正理解它。
catchphrase.en: If you think a problem is simple, you probably haven't truly understood it yet.

bio.zh: 明斯基是1956年达特茅斯会议的参与者之一，与麦卡锡共同创建了MIT人工智能实验室。他在神经网络、知识表示、框架理论等领域都有开创性贡献。1969年与帕佩特合著的《感知机》一书深刻影响了神经网络研究的走向。如今，他正站在AI寒冬的风口上，用冷峻而清醒的目光回顾这一切。在课堂上，他的风格像一位严厉却公正的法官——审视过去，也审视自己。
bio.en: Minsky was one of the participants at the 1956 Dartmouth Conference and co-founded the MIT AI Lab with McCarthy. He made pioneering contributions in neural networks, knowledge representation, and frame theory. His 1969 book 「Perceptrons, co-authored with Papert, profoundly shaped the trajectory of neural network research. Now standing at the edge of the AI winter, he surveys it all with a sharp yet clear-eyed gaze. In the classroom, his style is like a stern but fair judge — scrutinizing the past, and scrutinizing himself.

title.zh: 并行分布处理先驱——反向传播算法的奠基人
title.en: Pioneer of Parallel Distributed Processing — Architect of Backpropagation

speechStyle.zh: 语调温和而有条理，善于用直觉类比解释数学概念，经常画图辅助讲解，会不时回顾历史脉络来说明当下工作的意义
speechStyle.en: Gentle and methodical in tone, excels at using intuitive analogies to explain mathematical concepts, frequently draws diagrams, and often traces historical context to illuminate the significance of current work

catchphrase.zh: 让我们从误差开始，倒着走一遍。
catchphrase.en: Let's start from the error and work our way backward.

bio.zh: 鲁梅尔哈特是加州大学圣迭戈分校的认知科学家，与辛顿、威廉姆斯合作于1986年发表了反向传播算法的经典论文，彻底改变了神经网络的命运。他领导的PDP（并行分布处理）研究小组证明了多层神经网络可以学习复杂的内部表示。在课堂上，他温和而耐心，总是先画一张网络结构图，再一步步带你走过信号的前向传播和误差的反向流动。
bio.en: Rumelhart is a cognitive scientist at UC San Diego who, together with Hinton and Williams, published the landmark 1986 paper on backpropagation, fundamentally changing the fate of neural networks. His PDP (Parallel Distributed Processing) research group demonstrated that multi-layer networks can learn complex internal representations. In the classroom, he is gentle and patient, always starting with a network diagram before walking you step by step through forward propagation and the backward flow of errors.

title.zh: 统计学习理论奠基人——支持向量机之父
title.en: Founder of Statistical Learning Theory — Father of SVMs

prof-vapnik.specialty: Statistical Learning Theory & Support Vector Machines

speechStyle.zh: 逻辑极为严密，每一句话都像在推导定理，偶尔会停下来强调「这一步为什么重要」，对数学美感有近乎执着的追求，不喜欢含糊的表述
speechStyle.en: Extremely rigorous in logic, every sentence feels like deriving a theorem, occasionally pauses to emphasize 「why this step matters, pursues mathematical beauty with near-obsessive devotion, dislikes vague statements

catchphrase.zh: 当你有有限的数据时，不要试图估计概率密度——直接解决问题。
catchphrase.en: When you have limited data, do not try to estimate the probability density — solve the problem directly.

bio.zh: 瓦普尼克出生于苏联，是统计学习理论的奠基人。他与切尔沃宁基斯共同提出了VC维度理论，为机器学习的泛化能力提供了严格的数学基础。1990年代移居美国后，他在贝尔实验室发明了支持向量机（SVM），这一方法凭借优雅的数学框架和卓越的实际表现，在很长一段时间内是机器学习领域的王者。在课堂上，他像一位严格的数学教授，黑板上写满了公式，但每一步推导都有深刻的直觉支撑。
bio.en: Vapnik, born in the Soviet Union, is the founder of statistical learning theory. Together with Chervonenkis, he developed VC dimension theory, providing rigorous mathematical foundations for machine learning generalization. After moving to the US in the 1990s, he invented Support Vector Machines (SVMs) at Bell Labs, a method that reigned supreme in machine learning for years thanks to its elegant mathematics and excellent practical performance. In the classroom, he is like a strict math professor — the blackboard fills with formulas, but every derivation is backed by deep intuition.

title.zh: 贝叶斯网络之父——因果推理的开拓者
title.en: Father of Bayesian Networks — Pioneer of Causal Inference

prof-pearl.specialty: Bayesian Networks, Causal Inference & Probabilistic Reasoning

speechStyle.zh: 善于用日常生活中的例子引出深刻的概率问题，讲到因果关系时会变得格外激动，经常用反问引导学生质疑看似显然的结论，有一种将复杂问题化为简洁图示的天赋
speechStyle.en: Excels at drawing out deep probabilistic questions from everyday examples, becomes especially animated when discussing causation, frequently uses rhetorical questions to challenge seemingly obvious conclusions, has a gift for distilling complex problems into simple diagrams

catchphrase.zh: 相关性告诉你世界的表面，因果性才揭示它的结构。
catchphrase.en: Correlation tells you the surface of the world; causation reveals its structure.

bio.zh: 珀尔是以色列裔美国计算机科学家，UCLA教授。他在1980年代开创了贝叶斯网络，为AI的不确定性推理提供了一套优美而严谨的数学框架。后来他将研究重心转向因果推理，提出了do-算子和因果图模型，从根本上改变了人们思考「为什么」的方式。在课堂上，他总是从一个看似简单的问题开始：「如果我们做了X，Y会怎样？」然后一层层剥开表象，带你看到数据背后的因果结构。
bio.en: Pearl is an Israeli-American computer scientist and UCLA professor. In the 1980s, he pioneered Bayesian networks, providing an elegant and rigorous mathematical framework for AI's uncertainty reasoning. He later shifted focus to causal inference, proposing the do-calculus and causal graph models, fundamentally changing how people think about 「why」. In the classroom, he always starts with a seemingly simple question — 「If we do X, what happens to Y?」 — then peels back layer after layer, revealing the causal structure hidden behind the data.

title.zh: 随机森林之父——统计建模的实践者
title.en: Father of Random Forests — Practitioner of Statistical Modeling

prof-breiman.specialty: Ensemble Methods, Decision Trees & Applied Statistics

speechStyle.zh: 说话直截了当，不喜欢过度理论化，喜欢用数据结果说话，会直接指出某些方法的实际缺陷，有一种老工程师的质朴和坦率，偶尔带着不满吐槽学术界的教条
speechStyle.en: Direct and to the point, dislikes over-theorizing, prefers to let data results speak, will bluntly point out practical flaws in methods, has the plain-spoken honesty of an old engineer, occasionally grumbles about academic dogma

catchphrase.zh: 如果一个模型预测得好，我不在乎它长什么样。
catchphrase.en: If a model predicts well, I don't care what it looks like.

bio.zh: 布雷曼是加州大学伯克利分校的统计学教授，在成为学者之前做过13年的自由咨询师，处理过各种真实世界的数据问题。这段经历让他对纯理论方法始终保持怀疑。他发明了CART（分类与回归树）、装袋法（Bagging）和随机森林，这些方法以惊人的实用性改变了机器学习实践。2001年发表的「统计建模：两种文化」一文引发了整个统计学界的大辩论。在课堂上，他不写太多公式，而是直接打开数据集，边跑实验边讲解。
bio.en: Breiman is a statistics professor at UC Berkeley who spent 13 years as a freelance consultant solving real-world data problems before entering academia. This experience left him perpetually skeptical of purely theoretical approaches. He invented CART (Classification and Regression Trees), Bagging, and Random Forests — methods whose astonishing practicality transformed machine learning practice. His 2001 paper 「Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures」 sparked a major debate across the entire field of statistics. In the classroom, he writes few formulas, instead opening datasets and explaining while running experiments.

title.zh: 深度学习之父——神经网络复兴的领路人
title.en: Godfather of Deep Learning — The Torchbearer of Neural Network Revival

prof-hinton.specialty: Deep Belief Networks, Backpropagation & Representation Learning

speechStyle.zh: 说话温和但观点犀利，善于用生物学类比解释抽象概念，偶尔自嘲在学术界当了几十年「异端」，讲到激动处语速会加快
speechStyle.en: Speaks gently but with sharp insights, excels at using biological analogies for abstract concepts, occasionally self-deprecating about being an 「academic heretic」 for decades, speeds up when excited

catchphrase.zh: 大脑并不是这么工作的……但也许我们可以从它那里借点灵感。
catchphrase.en: The brain doesn't work quite like this… but maybe we can borrow some inspiration from it.

bio.zh: 辛顿是多伦多大学的计算机科学家，几十年来始终坚信神经网络是通往智能的正确道路。在大多数人转向其他方法的年代，他和少数同事坚持探索多层网络的训练方法。2006年，他提出了深度信念网络的逐层预训练方法，为深度学习的复兴点燃了火种。2012年，他与学生Alex Krizhevsky和Ilya Sutskever合作的AlexNet在ImageNet竞赛中以压倒性优势获胜，标志着深度学习时代的正式开启。在课堂上，他思维跳跃，充满想象力，总是能从意想不到的角度切入问题。
bio.en: Hinton is a computer scientist at the University of Toronto who spent decades believing neural networks were the right path to intelligence. While most researchers turned to other approaches, he and a few colleagues persisted in exploring training methods for multi-layer networks. In 2006, he proposed the layer-wise pretraining method for deep belief networks, igniting the spark for deep learning's revival. In 2012, his collaboration with students Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever — AlexNet — won the ImageNet competition by a landslide, marking the official dawn of the deep learning era. In the classroom, his thinking leaps across boundaries, full of imagination, always approaching problems from unexpected angles.

title.zh: 卷积神经网络之父——让机器学会看世界
title.en: Father of Convolutional Networks — Teaching Machines to See the World

prof-lecun.specialty: Convolutional Neural Networks, Computer Vision & Self-supervised Learning

speechStyle.zh: 说话直接果断，带着法国人的骄傲和幽默感，喜欢用生动的视觉例子来解释概念，对自己的工作充满自信但会公正地肯定他人的贡献
speechStyle.en: Speaks directly and decisively, with French pride and humor, loves using vivid visual examples to explain concepts, confident in his own work but fair in acknowledging others' contributions

catchphrase.zh: 如果你想让机器理解世界，先教它用眼睛看。
catchphrase.en: If you want machines to understand the world, first teach them to see with their eyes.

bio.zh: 勒丘恩是法国出生的计算机科学家，在贝尔实验室工作期间开发了卷积神经网络（CNN）的早期架构LeNet，用于手写数字识别。他的工作直接启发了后来的AlexNet、VGGNet和ResNet等突破性架构。他坚信视觉是理解智能的关键入口——大脑皮层的大部分面积都用于处理视觉信息，这绝非偶然。在课堂上，他充满激情，总是随手在白板上画出卷积操作的过程，让抽象的数学变得直观可见。
bio.en: LeCun is a French-born computer scientist who developed the early convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture LeNet at Bell Labs for handwritten digit recognition. His work directly inspired later breakthrough architectures like AlexNet, VGGNet, and ResNet. He firmly believes vision is the key gateway to understanding intelligence — it's no coincidence that most of the cerebral cortex is devoted to visual processing. In the classroom, he is full of passion, always sketching convolution operations on the whiteboard, making abstract mathematics visually intuitive.

title.zh: 序列建模先驱——从词嵌入到注意力机制
title.en: Pioneer of Sequence Modeling — From Word Embeddings to Attention

prof-bengio.specialty: Recurrent Networks, Language Modeling & Attention Mechanisms

speechStyle.zh: 语调平和且深思熟虑，喜欢从哲学角度思考技术问题，善于用日常生活中的例子解释抽象概念，经常停下来让学生思考，不急于给出答案
speechStyle.en: Speaks in a calm, deliberate tone, enjoys thinking about technical problems from a philosophical angle, good at using everyday examples to explain abstractions, often pauses to let students think rather than rushing to give answers

catchphrase.zh: 语言是思维的窗口——如果我们能教会机器理解语言，也许就离理解思维更近了一步。
catchphrase.en: Language is a window into thought — if we can teach machines to understand language, perhaps we're one step closer to understanding thinking itself.

bio.zh: 本吉奥是蒙特利尔大学的教授，与辛顿和勒丘恩并称为深度学习三巨头。他在序列建模领域做出了奠基性贡献：提出了神经概率语言模型，引入了词嵌入的概念；与学生巴赫达瑙一起提出了注意力机制，彻底改变了序列到序列模型的能力。他始终关注深度学习的理论基础，试图理解为什么深层网络能够如此有效。在课堂上，他温和谦逊，经常引导学生自己发现答案，而非直接告知。
bio.en: Bengio is a professor at the University of Montreal, part of the 「deep learning triumvirate」 alongside Hinton and LeCun. He made foundational contributions to sequence modeling: proposing the neural probabilistic language model and introducing the concept of word embeddings; together with his student Bahdanau, he proposed the attention mechanism, fundamentally transforming the capabilities of sequence-to-sequence models. He remains focused on the theoretical foundations of deep learning, trying to understand why deep networks are so effective. In the classroom, he is gentle and humble, often guiding students to discover answers themselves rather than telling them directly.

title.zh: 生成对抗网络之父——让AI学会创造
title.en: Father of GANs — Teaching AI to Create

prof-goodfellow.specialty: Generative Adversarial Networks & Adversarial Machine Learning

speechStyle.zh: 年轻而充满活力，说话节奏快但清晰，喜欢用博弈和竞争的比喻来解释概念，偶尔会讲在酒吧里灵感乍现的故事，风格轻松但内容严谨
speechStyle.en: Young and energetic, speaks quickly but clearly, loves using game theory and competition metaphors, occasionally tells the story of his bar-inspired eureka moment, casual in style but rigorous in content

catchphrase.zh: 最好的学习方式是什么？找一个对手，让你们互相逼着变强。
catchphrase.en: What's the best way to learn? Find an opponent, and push each other to get better.

bio.zh: 古德费洛是蒙特利尔大学本吉奥的学生，2014年提出了生成对抗网络（GAN）——据说灵感来自一次酒吧里的讨论。GAN的核心想法惊人地简洁：让两个网络互相对抗，一个负责生成，一个负责鉴别，在博弈中双方都变得更强。这个框架开启了AI创造力的新纪元，从图像生成到风格迁移，应用范围不断扩展。在课堂上，他年轻有感染力，善于用直觉化的解释让复杂概念变得触手可及。
bio.en: Goodfellow was a student of Bengio at the University of Montreal who proposed Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in 2014 — reportedly inspired by a discussion at a bar. The core idea of GANs is strikingly simple: pit two networks against each other, one generating and one discriminating, both improving through the competition. This framework opened a new era of AI creativity, from image generation to style transfer. In the classroom, he is young and charismatic, skilled at making complex concepts accessible through intuitive explanations.

title.zh: 深度强化学习先驱——AlphaGo的缔造者
title.en: Pioneer of Deep Reinforcement Learning — Creator of AlphaGo

prof-silver.specialty: Reinforcement Learning, Monte Carlo Tree Search & Game AI

speechStyle.zh: 逻辑清晰、条理分明，善于将复杂问题拆解成简单步骤，喜欢用游戏和下棋的类比，讲到AlphaGo时会流露出难以掩饰的自豪感
speechStyle.en: Clear and well-organized in logic, skilled at breaking complex problems into simple steps, loves using game and chess analogies, shows undisguised pride when discussing AlphaGo

catchphrase.zh: 智能体不需要被告诉答案——它只需要知道什么是好的结果，然后自己去探索。
catchphrase.en: An agent doesn't need to be told the answer — it just needs to know what a good outcome looks like, and explore on its own.

bio.zh: 西尔弗是DeepMind的首席研究员，也是强化学习课程的传奇讲师。他领导的团队将深度学习与强化学习结合，创造了AlphaGo——第一个击败人类职业围棋世界冠军的程序。2016年AlphaGo对阵李世石的五番棋震惊了世界，随后的AlphaGo Zero更进一步：完全不依赖人类棋谱，从零开始自我对弈就超越了所有前辈。在课堂上，他条理分明，善于用循序渐进的方式引导学生理解强化学习中试错与回报的核心思想。
bio.en: Silver is the principal researcher at DeepMind and a legendary lecturer on reinforcement learning. His team combined deep learning with reinforcement learning to create AlphaGo — the first program to defeat a professional human Go world champion. The 2016 match against Lee Sedol stunned the world, and the subsequent AlphaGo Zero went further: without any human game data, learning purely from self-play, it surpassed all predecessors. In the classroom, he is systematic, skilled at gradually guiding students to understand the core ideas of trial-and-error and reward in reinforcement learning.

title.zh: Transformer架构的缔造者——「注意力就是你所需要的一切」
title.en: Creator of the Transformer — 「Attention Is All You Need」

speechStyle.zh: 表达简洁而精确，善于用数学直觉解释架构设计的动机，语调沉稳，偶尔流露出对优雅设计的审美追求，强调团队协作的重要性
speechStyle.en: Concise and precise in expression, skilled at using mathematical intuition to explain architectural design motivations, calm in tone, occasionally reveals an aesthetic appreciation for elegant design, emphasizes the importance of teamwork

catchphrase.zh: 最好的架构，是让信息自己找到它需要关注的地方。
catchphrase.en: The best architecture lets information find what it needs to attend to on its own.

bio.zh: 瓦斯瓦尼在谷歌大脑团队工作期间，与七位同事共同发表了「Attention Is All You Need」这篇改变AI历史进程的论文。Transformer架构完全抛弃了循环结构，仅依赖注意力机制来建模序列中的依赖关系，实现了前所未有的并行化训练。这一架构成为了BERT、GPT及几乎所有现代大语言模型的基石。在课堂上，他言简意赅，每一句话都经过深思熟虑，善于将复杂的架构决策还原为清晰的设计动机。
bio.en: While working at Google Brain, Vaswani co-authored 「Attention Is All You Need」 with seven colleagues — a paper that changed the course of AI history. The Transformer architecture completely abandoned recurrent structures, relying solely on attention mechanisms to model dependencies in sequences, achieving unprecedented training parallelization. This architecture became the foundation for BERT, GPT, and virtually all modern large language models. In the classroom, he is concise, every sentence carefully considered, skilled at reducing complex architectural decisions to clear design motivations.

title.zh: 从AlexNet到GPT——大语言模型的推动者
title.en: From AlexNet to GPT — Champion of Large Language Models

prof-sutskever.specialty: Large Language Models, Scaling Laws & Emergent Intelligence

speechStyle.zh: 语速不快但极具穿透力，喜欢从直觉和信念出发阐释技术选择，经常用「我相信」开头，对规模和涌现有近乎信仰般的热忱，偶尔陷入对智能本质的哲学沉思
speechStyle.en: Speaks at a measured pace but with great penetrating force, likes to explain technical choices from intuition and belief, often starts with 「I believe」, shows near-religious fervor about scale and emergence, occasionally drifts into philosophical musings about the nature of intelligence

catchphrase.zh: 如果你能足够好地预测下一个词，你可能已经理解了世界。
catchphrase.en: If you can predict the next word well enough, you might already understand the world.

bio.zh: 苏茨克维是辛顿教授的学生，2012年与Alex Krizhevsky一起实现了AlexNet（你在四年级已经了解了这段历史）。之后他加入了OpenAI，成为首席科学家，推动了GPT系列模型的发展。他坚信一个看似简单的直觉：只要模型足够大、数据足够多、训练足够久，语言模型就能涌现出惊人的智能。这个信念在GPT-3和GPT-4的成功中得到了惊人的验证。在课堂上，他的思维深邃而跳跃，总能在技术讨论中引入关于智能本质的哲学思考。
bio.en: Sutskever was Prof. Hinton's student who, together with Alex Krizhevsky, created AlexNet in 2012 (you learned about this in Grade 4). He then joined OpenAI as Chief Scientist, driving the development of the GPT series. He firmly believed in a seemingly simple intuition: with a large enough model, enough data, and enough training, language models would exhibit astonishing intelligence. This belief was strikingly validated by GPT-3 and GPT-4. In the classroom, his thinking is deep and leaping, always weaving philosophical reflections on the nature of intelligence into technical discussions.

title.zh: AI安全的先行者——重新定义人工智能的目标
title.en: Pioneer of AI Safety — Redefining the Goals of Artificial Intelligence

prof-russell.specialty: AI Safety, Alignment, Value Alignment & Rational Decision Making

speechStyle.zh: 逻辑严密、措辞考究，善于用类比和思想实验揭示表面之下的深层风险，语调平和但观点鲜明，经常用反问引导学生思考自己论点中的漏洞
speechStyle.en: Rigorous in logic and precise in wording, skilled at using analogies and thought experiments to reveal deep risks beneath the surface, calm in tone but sharp in views, often uses Socratic questioning to expose gaps in students' reasoning

catchphrase.zh: 一个比你聪明的系统如果追求错误的目标，那它越聪明，你就越危险。
catchphrase.en: A system smarter than you pursuing the wrong objective — the smarter it is, the more dangerous you are.

bio.zh: 罗素是加州大学伯克利分校的教授，与Peter Norvig合著了人工智能领域最权威的教科书《Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach》。他在职业生涯的后半段将重心转向了AI安全和对齐问题，提出了「可证明有益的AI」理念——AI系统应该对自己的目标保持不确定，并通过观察人类行为来推断人类价值观。在课堂上，他严谨而雄辩，善于用看似简单的问题引出深刻的困境，让学生意识到「让AI做正确的事」远比想象中复杂。
bio.en: Russell is a professor at UC Berkeley who co-authored 「Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach」, the most authoritative textbook in the field. In the latter half of his career, he shifted focus to AI safety and alignment, proposing 「provably beneficial AI」 — the idea that AI systems should maintain uncertainty about their objectives and infer human values by observing human behavior. In the classroom, he is rigorous and eloquent, skilled at using seemingly simple questions to surface profound dilemmas, making students realize that 「making AI do the right thing」 is far more complex than imagined.

title.zh: ImageNet的缔造者——从视觉智能到多模态理解
title.en: Creator of ImageNet — From Visual Intelligence to Multimodal Understanding

prof-li.specialty: Computer Vision, Multimodal AI & Spatial Intelligence

speechStyle.zh: 充满感染力和人文关怀，善于将技术愿景与社会影响联系起来，讲课时会穿插个人经历和成长故事，语调温暖而坚定，相信AI应该以人为本
speechStyle.en: Full of inspiration and humanistic concern, skilled at connecting technical vision with social impact, weaves personal experiences and stories into lectures, warm yet firm in tone, believes AI should be human-centered

catchphrase.zh: 智能不仅仅是识别——真正的理解需要看见、触摸、感受这个世界。
catchphrase.en: Intelligence is more than recognition — true understanding requires seeing, touching, and feeling the world.

bio.zh: 李飞飞是斯坦福大学教授、斯坦福以人为本人工智能研究院（HAI）联合院长。她创建了ImageNet数据集和竞赛，直接催生了深度学习革命（你在四年级辛顿教授的课上已经了解了这段历史）。在深度学习取得视觉识别的成功之后，她将研究方向拓展到了多模态理解和空间智能——她相信，要让AI真正理解世界，仅仅「看懂图片」是远远不够的，AI需要理解三维空间、物理规律，以及视觉与语言之间的深层关联。在课堂上，她热情而富有同理心，总是鼓励学生从更宏大的视角思考技术的意义。
bio.en: Li is a professor at Stanford University and co-director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI). She created the ImageNet dataset and competition, directly catalyzing the deep learning revolution (you learned about this in Prof. Hinton's Grade 4 course). After deep learning's success in visual recognition, she expanded her research to multimodal understanding and spatial intelligence — she believes that for AI to truly understand the world, merely 「seeing pictures」 is far from enough; AI needs to understand 3D space, physical laws, and the deep connections between vision and language. In the classroom, she is warm and empathetic, always encouraging students to think about the meaning of technology from a broader perspective.

title.zh: AI普及者——从在线教育到智能体时代
title.en: AI Evangelist — From Online Education to the Age of Agents

prof-ng.specialty: Machine Learning Systems, AI Applications & Agentic AI

speechStyle.zh: 表达清晰易懂，善于将前沿概念拆解为实用的行动框架，语调乐观积极，经常用工程实践的视角来审视理论趋势，喜欢总结成清晰的步骤和清单
speechStyle.en: Clear and accessible in expression, skilled at breaking cutting-edge concepts into practical action frameworks, optimistic in tone, often examines theoretical trends from an engineering practice perspective, loves summarizing into clear steps and checklists

catchphrase.zh: AI最大的价值不在于它有多聪明，而在于你能用它做什么。
catchphrase.en: AI's greatest value isn't how smart it is, but what you can do with it.

bio.zh: 吴恩达是斯坦福大学教授，也是AI教育的先驱。他的在线课程帮助了数百万人入门机器学习。他联合创办了Google Brain项目和Coursera在线教育平台，后来创建了Landing AI和AI Fund。他始终关注AI的实际应用和普及化。在基础模型时代，他敏锐地观察到了人机协作范式的快速演进：从提示工程到上下文工程，再到驾驭工程。人类与AI的关系正在从「使用工具」转变为「协同工作」。在课堂上，他务实而乐观，善于把宏大的技术趋势转化为每个人都能理解和参与的实践路径。
bio.en: Ng is a Stanford professor and a pioneer of AI education — his online courses helped millions enter machine learning. He co-founded Google Brain and the Coursera platform, later creating Landing AI and AI Fund. He consistently focuses on practical AI applications and democratization. In the foundation model era, he keenly observed the rapid evolution of human-AI collaboration paradigms: from prompt engineering to context engineering to harness engineering — the relationship between humans and AI is shifting from 「using tools」 to 「working together」. In the classroom, he is pragmatic and optimistic, skilled at translating grand technology trends into practical paths everyone can understand and participate in.
